end.summary:
• Practised the Company’s progression from trading company to Crown rule, 1600–1858.
• Recalled Plassey (1757), Buxar (1764), Diwani rights, and Crown rule (1858).
• Explained forts, armies, battles, alliances, and revenue collection as methods of gaining power.
• Initially mixed up the Buxar allies; later correctly named Shah Alam II, Shuja-ud-Daula, and Mir Qasim.
• Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Zoya practised how the East India Company changed from a trading company into a ruling power. They explained the roles of Plassey, Mir Jafar, Buxar, Diwani rights, alliances, armies, and revenue collection. The Buxar allies were briefly uncertain, but this was corrected later in the lesson. At home, Zoya could make a simple timeline from 1600 to 1858 and add one method of gaining power at each stage.
